title: Alex Slater on Quitter: stepping back, firing the team, and revenue rising anyway
summary: Alex Slater updates on Quitter after 20 days back: steady $9-10k proceeds days, rising LTV and ARPU, after he cut a 14-person team. He explains how he tests whether he is the bottleneck, works directly on paywalls and content, and holds a high bar on his own content.

principles.text: Step away from your company to test whether you are the bottleneck.
principles.quote: I took a step back to see if I was the issue. Um spoiler, I wasn't the issue.

principles.text: A bloated team can be dead weight; cutting headcount can raise revenue rather than lower it.
principles.quote: we fired everyone and the revenue went up. It didn't go down, it went up.

principles.text: As founder, work directly on the paywall and the content, improving them to your own taste.
principles.quote: getting behind the scenes looking at the pay walls improving them based on what I want

principles.text: Make content you yourself want to watch.
principles.quote: going into the content and making content that I want to watch

principles.text: Track unit economics like LTV and ARPU as the real signal of health.
Hold a high quality bar and skip posting mediocre content, even if it is ready to ship.
principles.quote: I'm just not content with mediocre content.
